apiTones.title: '02 Vox AC30/6 Top Boost
apiTones.description: A 2002 Vox AC30/6 Top Boost captured through the Brilliant and Normal channels at a range of volume settings. The Brl (Brilliant) models run the Top Boost tone stack with the cut control at noon; the Nrm models are the flatter Normal channel. Recorded with a Suhr Reactive Load and a matched-level reamp, so the input calibration metadata is included: set your interface to 12.5 dBu for 0 dBFS and the model responds like the amp did.

updatePayload.message_html: New in 1.5.0: per-block EQ curve view, stereo chain branching, and lower CPU on Apple Silicon.

data.title: '02 Vox AC30/6 Top Boost
data.description: A 2002 Vox AC30/6 Top Boost captured through the Brilliant and Normal channels at a range of volume settings. The Brl (Brilliant) models run the Top Boost tone stack with the cut control at noon; the Nrm models are the flatter Normal channel. Recorded with a Suhr Reactive Load and a matched-level reamp, so the input calibration metadata is included: set your interface to 12.5 dBu for 0 dBFS and the model responds like the amp did.

scenarios.title: Signal chain - mono
scenarios.description: The default view. A mono chain with three tone blocks (drive pedal, amp, cab IR) and two open + slots. Input/output meters flank the gallery; the faceplate carries global gain, gate and tone stack; the hint bar sits at the bottom.

scenarios.title: Signal chain - hot meters (clip latched)
scenarios.description: Input at 0 dBFS latches the clip LED (topmost dot) red; the output column lights to -3. Hovering the lit LED shows the clip hint; clicking it clears the latch.

scenarios.title: Signal chain - empty
scenarios.description: A fresh instance before any tone is loaded: five empty + slots. Clicking any + opens the TONE3000 browser (signing in first if needed).

scenarios.title: Block detail card
scenarios.description: Clicking a tile opens the block detail takeover: artwork, model picker with prev/next, In/Out/Mix knobs, per-block meters, and the header row with EQ, share, swap, power and remove. This NAM block carries calibration metadata (gauge next to the title).

scenarios.title: Block detail - info view
scenarios.description: The (i) view: the artwork shrinks beside the title column and the TONE3000 description (clamped, MORE expands), gear makes and tags load underneath; the card grows past the fixed height and the column scrolls to the faceplate.

scenarios.title: Block detail - info view, signed out
scenarios.description: Signed out, the info view has no catalog to read from: a Log In prompt replaces the description, and the model picker is disabled with a sign-in hint.

scenarios.title: Block EQ - slider view
scenarios.description: The per-block 6-band EQ opened from the detail card, in the gain-only fader view. The EQ pill in the header shows an outline when the EQ is actively shaping the sound.

scenarios.title: Block EQ - curve view
scenarios.description: The same EQ in the parametric curve view: draggable band dots over the live output spectrum, with freq/gain/Q chips per band.

scenarios.title: Block detail - model picker open
scenarios.description: The model dropdown on the detail card, paging through every model of the tone from the TONE3000 catalog. Signed-out users see the picker disabled with a sign-in hint instead.

scenarios.title: Signal chain - stereo, independent lanes
scenarios.description: Stereo mode: channel 0 feeds the Left lane, channel 1 the Right lane. Each lane has its own pan knob on the rail between them (linkable), and the faceplate gains Balance, Offset and the input-mode button.

scenarios.title: Signal chain - stereo, branched
scenarios.description: A branch: the Right lane taps its input from the Left lane after the amp block (elbow + indent). Used for wet/dry rigs and parallel cab setups. Clicking the junction makes the chains independent again.

scenarios.title: Tuner - no signal
scenarios.description: The chromatic tuner replaces the middle band (toggled from the header). With no input signal the note readout and bars sit dimmed.

scenarios.title: Tuner - in tune
scenarios.description: Within +-5 cents both center bars and both triangles light up blue.

scenarios.title: Tuner - flat
scenarios.description: Flat notes light the left bars; the further off, the more bars.

scenarios.title: Tuner - sharp
scenarios.description: Sharp notes light the right bars.

scenarios.title: Tuner - accidental
scenarios.description: Sharps hang the accidental off the right of the letter so the letter stays centered.

scenarios.title: Block downloading (gallery)
scenarios.description: A tile while its model file downloads from TONE3000: loading dots over the artwork. The second block here is mid-download; audio passes through until the model is ready.

scenarios.title: Block downloading (detail card)
scenarios.description: The same download state on the open detail card.

scenarios.title: Block download failed (detail card)
scenarios.description: The failed state on the detail card. Retry re-queues the download; when signed in the session token is refreshed first.

scenarios.title: Offline modal
scenarios.description: Clicking any internet-dependent action (+ slot, swap, login) with no network interface up opens this gate. It is an instant navigator.onLine check; a connected-but-dead network instead lands on the failed-download / OAuth recovery paths.

scenarios.title: Offline with cached models
scenarios.description: No network, but every model in the chain is already downloaded: the rig keeps playing normally. Tone artwork cannot be fetched, so tiles fall back to their gear-type icons; everything else works until an action needs the internet.

scenarios.title: OAuth - leaving for TONE3000
scenarios.description: The busy scrim shown the instant a login/browse hand-off to tone3000.com kicks off, so the UI never sits interactive while the system browser opens.

scenarios.title: OAuth - returning from TONE3000
scenarios.description: Landing back from tone3000.com with an authorization code: the busy overlay covers the chain while tokens are exchanged and the picked tone is resolved.

scenarios.title: OAuth - failed (recovery overlay)
scenarios.description: When a navigation to tone3000.com fails (offline, site down), native reloads the plugin UI with an error marker and the user lands on this overlay with Try Again / Dismiss instead of a dead page.

scenarios.title: Update available
scenarios.description: Startup update check against the TONE3000 version endpoint (best effort, never blocks). Remind me later snoozes for 1/7/30 days; the update also stays visible in Settings while snoozed.

version.message_html: New in 1.5.0: per-block EQ curve view, stereo chain branching, and lower CPU on Apple Silicon.

scenarios.title: Banner - microphone access denied
scenarios.description: macOS privacy is blocking audio input entirely; the device opens but the stream is silent. Highest priority and not dismissable; the action jumps to the OS privacy page.

scenarios.title: Banner - no audio input
scenarios.description: No input device selected (or no active input channel): the plugin cannot hear the instrument.

scenarios.title: Banner - device disconnected
scenarios.description: Same rule as no-input, but the wording flips when the device failed to open or was unplugged.

scenarios.title: Banner - no audio output
scenarios.description: A device is open but nothing is routed out, so the plugin is inaudible.

scenarios.title: Banner - input muted (by the user)
scenarios.description: Hear Yourself is off while an input is active, so the user hears nothing.

scenarios.title: Banner - input muted to prevent feedback
scenarios.description: The app auto-muted because a microphone is feeding speakers; different copy pointing at headphones/interface.

scenarios.title: Banner - feedback risk
scenarios.description: Monitoring is on with a mic-into-speakers setup: nothing is muted but a squeal is one gain bump away. Dismissable.

scenarios.title: Banner - ASIO available (Windows)
scenarios.description: An ASIO driver reports devices while a slower Windows driver type is current.

scenarios.title: Banner - large buffer latency
scenarios.description: Buffer above 512 samples with a smaller option available: nudges toward a more responsive setting.

scenarios.title: Banner - not running at 48 kHz
scenarios.description: Informational, lowest priority: off 48 kHz the chain resamples and burns a little more CPU.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - search (signed in)
scenarios.description: The Select tone screen: search box, the filter button, the verified and Profile chips, and the gear chips over the trending catalog.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - clearing a chip closes its open menu
scenarios.description: Sort set to Newest, its menu reopened, then the chip's × pressed: the sort is back to Trending and the menu is gone; any filter change closes an open menu.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - window at 1.3x, the body holds 1x
scenarios.description: The ← row zooms with the window; everything under it does not. The search box, filter row and cards keep their 1x height and widen to fill the column, so the bigger window shows more of the page.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - window at 1.6x, three columns
scenarios.description: Once three cards fit at their default width (800 x 1.6 = 1280 >= 3 x 392 + 2 x 16) the grid goes three-up.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - window at 1.6x, a filter menu
scenarios.description: A popover takes its anchor's scale: the Sort menu opened from the 1x filter row is 1x too, sitting under its chip.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - signed out
scenarios.description: The whole screen needs a TONE3000 session: signed out it shows only the sign-in prompt.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - loading
scenarios.description: The loading dots while the first search is in flight and there is nothing to keep on screen.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - nothing found
scenarios.description: A search with no results: the empty copy under the untouched filters.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - search failed
scenarios.description: A failed search (TONE3000 unreachable, 5xx): error copy plus Try again.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - loading a picked tone
scenarios.description: After clicking a card the grid dims and the card gets a busy overlay while the tone and its first model resolve; the tone then lands in the chain.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - results scrolled under the filter row
scenarios.description: The grid scrolled most of a row: cards run into a solid band of black under the pills, then fade out fast, so they never look like they touch the filters.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - search text
scenarios.description: Enter submits the text; the × on the right clears it and submits again.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - gear chip
scenarios.description: A gear chip narrows the catalog to that type; the active chip reads white.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - verified creators
scenarios.description: The verified chip keeps only tones from verified creators (badge beside their names).

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Profile menu
scenarios.description: The Profile chip lists the signed-in user's own streams: Recently used, Favorites, Created.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Recently used
scenarios.description: A profile filter set: the chip shows it with an ×, and the catalog-only filters park (those streams take a title search and gear alone; the search box stays live).

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Search within a profile
scenarios.description: Recently used with "vox" typed: the stream endpoints take a title search, so the box narrows the user's own list; gear chips still apply, the parked filters don't.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - empty profile stream
scenarios.description: Favorites with no tones yet (fresh account): stream-specific empty copy.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - more filters
scenarios.description: The filter button unfolds the catalog filters (sort, format, tags, makes, creators, calibrated) ahead of the rest of the row.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Sort menu
scenarios.description: The Sort chip's menu: Trending, Popular, Newest, Oldest (Best match joins while there is search text). The sort in force reads white, no check; Trending is the default, so the chip stays gray on it.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Format: IR
scenarios.description: A format picked: the chip shows it with an × and the results narrow to impulse responses.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Tags menu
scenarios.description: A taxonomy menu: a search field over the most-used names from the API.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - tags picked
scenarios.description: A pick closes the menu and narrows the results; reopened, the chosen tags lead the list ticked. The chip lists them with an ×.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Sort set
scenarios.description: Newest picked: the Sort chip names it in white with an × back to the default, and the filters button would carry the dot once folded.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Calibrated parked under IR gear
scenarios.description: Cabinet picked with the filters expanded: cabinets are impulse responses with no calibration data, so the Calibrated chip dims and the flag is left out of the request. The divider parts the extra filters from the ones always shown.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Format menu
scenarios.description: Both formats read gray until one is picked; the panel is wide enough for the full names.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - Creators menu
scenarios.description: Creator rows lead with the avatar (the person glyph when there is none), as on the cards.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - back where it was left
scenarios.description: Leave with a gear chip set and come back: the query, filter row and results are retained for the session, with no fetch.

scenarios.title: Tone browser - filters set, collapsed
scenarios.description: Back from the catalog filters with some set: the filter button reads white with a dot.

scenarios.title: Plugin Settings (in a DAW)
scenarios.description: Hosted builds get a single page: Info Bar toggle, MIDI Mapping and Advanced entry points, the update row when a newer version exists, and the running version in the footer.

version.message_html: New in 1.5.0: per-block EQ curve view, stereo chain branching, and lower CPU on Apple Silicon.

scenarios.title: Plugin Settings - Advanced
scenarios.description: NAM A2 size (LITE/FULL), per-block normalization, input calibration with its dBu field, oversampling with rate picker, multi-core stereo, and diagnostics (copy/reveal logs).

scenarios.title: MIDI Mapping - empty
scenarios.description: No mappings yet: explainer copy plus the control picker.

scenarios.title: MIDI Mapping - mappings + learn armed
scenarios.description: Learned CC/note assignments with re-learn / remove buttons, a channel filter, and a target armed for learn waiting for the next hardware move (or a typed CC number).

scenarios.title: MIDI Mapping - choosing a control
scenarios.description: The target picker open: every mappable control with its context (presets, global knobs, and a power toggle per chain slot named after the tone currently in it). Picking one arms learn.

scenarios.title: System Settings (standalone)
scenarios.description: The standalone app adds this tab: driver/device pickers, input channel selection with live meters, Hear Yourself, test tone, buffer and sample rate, and MIDI hardware inputs.

scenarios.title: System Settings - mic access denied
scenarios.description: The banner rules render inline in the settings form too: here the mic-permission error with its Allow Access action.

scenarios.title: System Settings - feedback risk
scenarios.description: Hear Yourself is on with a mic-into-speakers setup, so the feedback warning renders inline under the toggle that causes it (same copy as the main-window banner).

scenarios.title: System Settings - input muted to prevent feedback
scenarios.description: The auto-mute state inline: Hear Yourself is off because a microphone is feeding speakers, with the copy pointing at headphones or an interface.

scenarios.title: System Settings - sample rate warning
scenarios.description: Scrolled down to Buffer Size / Sample Rate / MIDI Inputs. Running off 48 kHz puts the informational rate notice inline under the picker.

scenarios.title: Account menu - signed out
scenarios.description: Hamburger + avatar pill; signed out it offers Settings and Login.

scenarios.title: Account menu - signed in
scenarios.description: Signed in the avatar comes from the TONE3000 profile and Logout replaces Login.

scenarios.title: Preset save popover
scenarios.description: Saving stores the whole chain + faceplate under a name; a same-name user preset is overwritten.

scenarios.title: Preset browser
scenarios.description: Factory (TONE3000) and user sections with search; user presets get rename/delete on hover, and the reorder toggle swaps those for move up/down.

scenarios.title: Toast - Preset Saved
scenarios.description: The app-wide toast pill above the faceplate; also used for Link Copied (share), and the auto-measure results.

scenarios.title: Spread enabled (mono)
scenarios.description: In mono, Spread doubles the chain into an ADT-style stereo image: the faceplate group expands to Offset + Wobble knobs, power button, and the mono-safety correlation LED. The output meter and Balance switch to their stereo forms.

scenarios.title: Gate advanced deck
scenarios.description: Right-clicking the Gate group (knob or power) opens the gate deck above the plate, anchored to the knob: Release, Hold and Range knobs, no power switches. Every knob sits at its default (50 ms, 20 ms, 80 dB), so a stock rig reads unchanged.

scenarios.title: Spread advanced deck
scenarios.description: Right-clicking the Spread group opens the shared deck panel above the plate: Wobble and Crossover knobs with their power buttons, the Diffuse power, and the mono-safety correlation LED. Spread defaults every section on.

scenarios.title: Align advanced deck (advert state)
scenarios.description: With Align off, right-clicking the ALIGN advert still opens its deck, flush-right to the group. Align defaults every section off, so the knobs render dimmed.

scenarios.title: Auto-balance listening
scenarios.description: Clicking the auto button next to Balance arms a ~2 s measurement: the pinned Listening toast stays up while the user plays, then the matched trim lands as a toast.

scenarios.title: Input mode menu
scenarios.description: With a real stereo source feeding the plugin, the faceplate input button picks what enters the chain: both channels, or left/right mirrored onto both. Session state, not preset state.

scenarios.title: Tile context menu
scenarios.description: Right-clicking a tone tile offers Copy (tone, model and all settings); right-clicking a + slot offers Paste when a copied block is on the clipboard.

scenarios.title: Hint bar hidden
scenarios.description: The info bar can be turned off (X on the bar or the Settings toggle); the window shrinks by its height rather than stretching the UI.
